items.title: SN 1106: ARTEX - Agentic AI-Driven Cyberattacks Are Happening at Scale
items.author: feedmail@twit.tv (TWiT Editors)
items.content:
AI-powered pen testing frameworks like ARTEX are now fueling real-world cyberattacks at unprecedented speed and scale, making the internet actively hostile for organizations of every size. Steve and Leo both examine the chilling reality of automated, always-on adversaries and the constant scramble to keep up.

  • An overview of the past several weeks of widespread outages
  • The "Reverse Engineer Anything" craze hits a road bump.
  • Quad9 withdraws its DNS service from France. What's next?
  • California sues OpenAI over Hugging Face and more.
  • More critical vulnerabilities in Synology.
  • PHP vulnerabilities, round two.
  • Google and Anthropic reduce their disclosure windows.
  • A listener uses Mythos, discovers unexpected bugs.
  • SpinRite boots on 97 different UEFI PCs.
  • ARTEX - The inevitable happened, and it's bad.

items.title: SN 1105: Formal Code Verification - When All Your Apps Go Dark
items.author: feedmail@twit.tv (TWiT Editors)
items.content:
What if AI could finally prove your code is bug-free? A new advance out of MIT and Google DeepMind is redefining what's possible in software verification—and it could mean a future with provably correct code, not just wishful thinking.

  • Last week's Microsoft 365 and FAA nationwide ground stops.
  • Riding the Patch Tuesday rollercoaster.
  • Speaking of Patch Tuesday: the return of Nightmare Eclipse.
  • Synology patches a critical 9.8 remote authentication flaw.
  • The unexpected revocation of GRC's code signing certificate.
  • "Weight-space programming" and its implication for AI.
  • SpinRite for UEFI progress report.
  • Why only encrypting every third block is not okay.
  • The holy grail of Formal Code Verification

items.title: SN 1104: The hole in OpenSSH - Password Bypass in Plain Sight
items.author: feedmail@twit.tv (TWiT Editors)
items.content:
From hacked French refrigerators igniting fires to a massive OpenSSH authentication bug hiding in plain sight for a decade, this week's stories expose how lapses in basic security ripple into chaos—and why AI is now both a weapon and shield.

  • TA surprising announcement regarding SpinRite.
  • What is being "AI-pilled" and how does it happen.
  • OpenAI just released GPT-6 Cyber. What does that mean.
  • An irresponsible hacker published 30+ N-Able 0-days.
  • 700 French refrigerators hacked. What's next.
  • Lots of listener feedback about the Cloudflare tunneling solution, Voyager 1, true hardware drive encryption, the random number 4 and the amount of debris in orbit
  • Then we look at a 10-year old serious SSH authentication bug (that's kinda wonderful)

items.title: SN 1103: Exposing Bad Consumer Crypto - AI vs. Encrypted Drives
items.author: feedmail@twit.tv (TWiT Editors)
items.content:
What happens when a 27-year-old gets handed the keys to completely refactor nearly all of Cisco's code? This week's episode dives into tech's strangest management bets and the friction brewing inside one of the industry's giants.

  • Cisco gives a 27-year old the task of recoding 98% of their software with AI.
  • A serious but not earth shaking vulnerability found in PXE booting.
  • The largest ($6.3 BILLION) financial heist in history (with crypto).
  • 710 Polymarket gambling wallets emptied of $2.7 million.
  • A new robots.txt control for AI bots, and agreement to obey it.
  • Google generates haiku from the first orbital AI.
  • From our listeners: Does stealth updating make sense, how to move web servers off the Internet, books don't contain knowledge, a small company attacked by powerful AI, how would an "AI kill switch" be implemented.
  • Another new and worrisome application of reverse-engineering AI
